what_was_built.pdf: kb.catalog.parsers.pdf — pypdf 6.20.0. parse_pdf(data, source_id) returns one Fragment per file page, the page's ProcessingStatus, and a tuple of named problems. file_page is the 1-based position read from the page tree; printed_label is filled ONLY when the document declares a /PageLabels number tree, because pypdf's own answer for a document that declares none is the page position wearing a label's clothes, and recording that would make the printed_label column corroborate file_page instead of disagreeing with it. A label found in the page's text is a guess about layout and is not attempted.
what_was_built.epub: kb.catalog.parsers.epub — EbookLib 0.18 for the container, stdlib html.parser for the body. One Fragment per text block, in reading order: kind=epub_chapter, spine=<1-based position in the OPF spine>, chapter=<the title the book's own TOC states, else None>, paragraph=<1-based block index in that document>. Block elements are p, li, blockquote, pre, h1-h6, td, th, dt, dd, figcaption; head/title, nav, script, style and svg are not book text. No fragment carries file_page or printed_label, ever.
what_was_built.shared: Both modules return kb.contracts.entities.Fragment — the same contract the HTTP and MCP surfaces use — and both offer fragment_row() for the kb.fragment columns, text_at_locator() to re-open a file at a locator, and a result object carrying the parser name and its exact version.
what_was_built.locator_shape: Locator(file_page=3, printed_label='1', kind=pdf_file_page) is the intended shape for a page that has both. The schema's pdf_printed_label kind is for a label that is all you have; it cannot carry a file_page, by CHECK and by the contract, and the tests make the server's refusal visible rather than working around it.

test_no_ocr_library_is_imported_by_the_parser — an AST import walk plus call-shaped needles; the first version of this test banned the bare text 'ocr(' and failed on the module's own needs_ocr property, which is recorded because a textual ban that wide proves nothing
central_invariant.mutation_tested: ten mutations were injected and reverted; each was rejected by at least one named test. (1) printed_label falling back to the file page when no /PageLabels tree is declared — failed test_a_document_that_declares_no_labels_gets_no_labels. (2) a textless page producing a placeholder fragment '[no text layer on this page]' — failed the needs_ocr tests and the ordinal test. (3) an all-image document reported DONE — failed test_a_page_less_scan_becomes_needs_ocr_and_not_invented_text. (4) ordinal taken from the fragment count instead of the page position — failed the mixed-scan test. (5) an ambiguous printed label resolving to the first match — failed test_a_printed_label_several_pages_share_is_not_guessed. (6) a missing chapter title filled in from the document's first heading — failed two EPUB chapter tests. (7) spine positions counted from zero — failed the spine test. (8) an EPUB paragraph given file_page and a pdf_file_page kind — failed four EPUB tests. (9) an image-only book reported DONE — failed the EPUB needs_ocr test. (10) the <title> element treated as body text — failed the parametrized block tests. No mutation tried survived.

checks.name: documents_this_card_cannot_cover
checks.reason: Two acknowledged limits, neither of which is a check that could have run here. (1) Fragment granularity is one per PDF page: pypdf exposes word and line coordinates, but kb.fragment has no column for them, so finer addressing would need a schema change outside this card. (2) The EPUB parser inherits EbookLib's container handling; a real-world EPUB that EbookLib 0.18 cannot open comes back FAILED with the library's own message rather than with a partial parse. Neither is covered by a real book, because no real book may be used as a fixture.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: kb.fragment has RLS enabled and FORCED with exactly one policy, fragment_read (SELECT). There is no INSERT policy, and 0002's blanket `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES TO kb_app` is then useless, because FORCE RLS applies to the runtime role as well. A contributor therefore cannot write a single fragment: the worker that will run this card's parsers has nowhere to put its output. This is the same class of gap C10 found and closed for kb.source_version in 0004.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: reported, not fixed: migrations/ is single-owner and outside this card. The gap is recorded by a test that is written to FAIL once the policy exists — test_there_is_no_fragment_write_policy_so_nobody_can_persist_a_fragment_yet asserts that a contributor's INSERT is refused with a row-level security error, so the integrator gets a signal rather than a silent change of behaviour. Also worth deciding in the same pass: kb_worker currently has no INSERT grant on kb.fragment at all (only SELECT on kb.source and SELECT/UPDATE on kb.job), so the fix needs both a policy and a grant.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: kb.fragment has no `spine` column, although locator_kind has an epub_spine value and the Locator contract has a `spine` field (typed as text). An EPUB fragment's reading-order position is therefore lost on write: the in-memory locator keeps it and text_at_locator uses it, but a stored row cannot say which of three spine documents a paragraph came from — only which chapter title, and two documents may share a title or have none.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: not worked around, and explicitly not patched by overloading `chapter` with the spine position, which would be a fabricated chapter name. fragment_row() documents the omission; test_the_spine_position_has_no_column_so_the_row_cannot_carry_it queries information_schema and is written to fail when the column appears. Proposed for the DDL owner: `spine integer CHECK (spine IS NULL OR spine >= 1)` on kb.fragment, mirroring the file_page CHECK style.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: The CHECK `printed_label_is_not_a_page` can never be the constraint PostgreSQL reports. Any row that violates it (kind = pdf_printed_label with a non-NULL file_page) also violates `file_page_requires_kind`, which is defined first and is checked first, so the server always names the latter. The guarantee is real — the row is refused — but the second CHECK is a redundant restatement rather than an independent guard, and a test written against its name would be asserting on something the server never says.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: measured, not assumed: the first run of test_the_database_refuses_a_printed_label_that_carries_a_file_page asserted on `printed_label_is_not_a_page` and failed with `file_page_requires_kind` in the server's message. The test now asserts the refusal and names the constraint the server actually reports, with the redundancy explained. No DDL change proposed: removing the redundant CHECK would lose a stated invariant without changing behaviour, and that is the owner's call.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: This card needs pypdf==6.20.0 and EbookLib==0.18 and cannot declare them: both files are single-owner. A venv built by `just prepare` today has neither, and every test in tests/integration/parsers/ fails at import. EbookLib 0.18 is also the last release of that project (2020) and is unmaintained; it pulls lxml==6.1.3 and six==1.17.0, and lxml is already required by python-docx, so another card's parser is in the same closure.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: installed into the shared venv and reported under dependencies_installed. The pin set, and any decision to replace EbookLib with a stdlib zipfile + ElementTree reader, belong to the lock owner. The arguments for keeping it: it is the real library the ecosystem uses for EPUB containers, and it handles META-INF/container.xml, the OPF manifest/spine and the NCX that a hand-rolled reader would have to reimplement. The argument against: it is unmaintained, and a single malformed package makes it raise where a tolerant reader could still return a partial parse.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: The bundler's docstring says real book content is excluded by policy, but the implementation has no rule for it — it excludes by directory, suffix and a small FORBIDDEN name list (keys, credentials, cookies). A committed real PDF or EPUB would be packaged silently. This card's fixtures are 24 KiB of generated bytes and are safe, and a test asserts that nothing in src/, migrations/ or deploy/ references them, but the policy is enforced only where the author remembers to enforce it.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: documented here rather than fixed: scripts/ is outside this card's allowed paths. A cheap owner-side fix is a rule excluding evals/ or a size threshold for binary files in the package tree.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: EbookLib 0.18's read_epub takes a path, not a stream, so the parser writes the bytes to a NamedTemporaryFile and deletes it. The file is created with the process umask in the system temp directory and removed in a finally block, so a crash between the two leaves an unreadable copy of a book on disk.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: kept, and bounded: the file lives only for the duration of one parse, is unlinked in a finally, and its name carries no title, no author and no source id. A directory the card controls would be better, but choosing a temp location is a product decision, not a parser's.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: A page's printed label is taken from the document's /PageLabels number tree only. A large class of real PDFs has no such tree and prints page numbers in the page header instead; for those, printed_label is always None even when the number is plainly visible. Detecting it would mean guessing from text position, which is the failure mode this card exists to prevent.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: deliberately not done, and the rule is stated in the module docstring and in test_a_document_that_declares_no_labels_gets_no_labels. If the product later wants header-derived labels, it needs a stated confidence per page and a human review path, not a parser default.

findings_for_the_next_owner.finding: The card's allowed test globs are pdf* and epub*, so there is no legal name in that directory for a shared conftest.py or db_support.py. The PostgreSQL runner and fixtures are therefore written out twice, once per file, and the two databases have to differ because CREATE POLICY and CREATE TRIGGER are not idempotent.
findings_for_the_next_owner.action_taken: accepted and explained in the epub_database_test.py docstring. Factoring the harness out needs one neutral path from the owner.
